decision.question: How to stop /ask/turn firing on every page load off localhost
options: leave the eager top-level probe and just catch() harder (does not stop Chrome's own console log for a 400 response)
make ask_probe a lazy memoized function, called only from a real user action (tabs.js open()) and from ask() itself when actually invoked, never at module import time
decision.chose: lazy memoized ask_probe(), triggered by open() and by ask()
decision.why: Chrome logs any 400/405 response to console itself, regardless of .catch() in JS, so the only way to get zero console errors on a passive page load is to never send the request until the user actually opens the drawer or asks something
decision.rule: minion#never-list (never edit outside fence) + code#7 (network calls that never throw still show up in devtools)

assign.title: AI 2 cards on a phone: no more /ask/turn console error
assign.outcome:
**Landed** — an AI 2 card opened from a phone on the LAN no longer logs a `POST /ask/turn -> 400` console error on page load.

- [x] find the caller: `ext/Ask/Ask.js`'s `ask_probe` was a top-level `fetch` that ran the instant the file was imported — which is every page, since `app.js` imports the drawer's ☰ menu unconditionally.
- [x] don't call it unless the user actually asks something: `ask_probe` is now a lazy, memoized function, called only from `ask()` (a real ask) and from `ext/drawer/tabs.js`'s `open()` (a real click on ☰) — never at module scope.
- [x] proof: headless Playwright load of `/framework/ai2/2026-09-29/ask-turn-quiet/` over the LAN address (`http://10.0.0.135:8137/`) at 400px — 0 console or network errors mentioning `/ask/turn`.

Changed: [`ext/Ask/Ask.js`](/framework/ext/Ask/), [`ext/drawer/tabs.js`](/framework/ext/drawer/). Commit `fb7aa793` on `michael/dev`. Left alone: the unrelated `/servex/card?id=...` 404 seen in the same test (Servex isn't running against this dev server) — not part of this fence.
